header_summary:
Mining of the testnet 5 genesis block is scheduled to coincide with the mainnet retarget event at block 975,744, incorporating several structural modifications for easier pooled mining and improved genesis block format, as detailed in [this pull request](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2347). Documentation and resources for participating miners are provided, including a [0%-fee solo-mining pool](https://lapis.erisian.com.au/chain.html), while ongoing tests and further discussions about block height encoding inconsistencies are available in related references. 

A comprehensive suite of five proposals—Tapleaf 0xc2—seeks to restore and expand Bitcoin Script capabilities by re-enabling previously disabled opcodes, introducing transaction introspection, and enforcing computational budgets, all while maintaining backward compatibility; the full specifications and reference implementations are accessible at [BIP 440](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0440.mediawiki), [BIP 441](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0441.mediawiki), and [the dedicated Bitcoin Core fork](https://github.com/bitcoin-gsr/bitcoin/tree/gsr). These changes enable advanced covenants, new cryptographic verification methods, and efficient Taproot outputs, but raise open questions regarding consensus risk and potential impacts on transaction ordering and Miner Extractable Value (MEV).

A new anti-exfiltration protocol has been proposed to prevent compromised signing devices from leaking sensitive information through manipulated nonces, with two draft BIPs specifying the protocol and new PSBT fields; resources and ongoing implementations can be found at [https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil](https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil) and [https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org](https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org). While several hardware wallet interfaces are experimenting with these standards, the protocol has yet to undergo formal cryptographic review, and peer feedback is actively solicited.

Decentralized mining pool discussions highlight persistent challenges and terminology standardization, while data from P2Pool illustrates natural limits on small miner participation due to payout structure and dust rules, as documented in a [CSV dataset](https://www.learnbitcoin.com/downloads/p2pool-coinbases.csv). Recent proposals to accumulate shares before payout aim to address dust creation, but robust, manipulation-resistant solutions remain under development. 

Finally, maintaining accurate tracking tools for Taproot support, such as [whentaproot.org](https://whentaproot.org/), is emphasized as critical, with updates reflecting changes in service adoption, including Binance’s confirmed Taproot withdrawals. Multi-party signing protocol design continues to evolve, with open questions on optimal agreement thresholds and operational security inviting expert analysis, as outlined in the comprehensive [signer group design note](https://github.com/davelund110/bolts/blob/39c63a434a3bf8add47f5812fc550f20d5e89ca8/signer-group-design-note.md).

recent_posts.title: Testnet 5 launch
recent_posts.summary: - Mining of testnet5 genesis block aligns with the mainnet retarget event at block 975,744.  - Genesis block structure changes simplify pooled mining and update block format for consistency.  - Block height encoding inconsistencies may cause issues during blockchain initialization with different mining software.

recent_posts.title: [Proposal] Tapleaf 0xc2: An overview of the Great Script Restoration (GSR)
recent_posts.summary: - A comprehensive upgrade proposes five interoperable changes to restore and expand advanced Bitcoin Script features.  - The initiative introduces transaction introspection, reusable macros, new primitives, covenants, and ensures backward compatibility.  - Static analysis is preserved, resource usage is budgeted, and community feedback on broader impacts is still required.

recent_posts.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields
recent_posts.summary: - A collaborative protocol reduces risk of device nonce manipulation by involving the host in generation and verification.  - Draft BIPs propose standardized anti-exfiltration processes, new PSBT fields, and compatibility with major signature schemes.  - Implementations exist but lack formal cryptographic review; peer feedback and further testing are requested.

recent_posts.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
recent_posts.summary: - Standardized terminology improved clarity and precision in discussions on decentralized mining pools and P2Pool.  - Network growth and technical constraints naturally limited small miners’ participation, squeezing them out over time.  - Proposed solutions and current research emphasize value-based selection and robust anti-manipulation mechanisms for payouts.

recent_posts.title: Should wallets default to Taproot or SegWit receive addresses while some services still reject bc1p?
recent_posts.summary: - The website helps track Taproot support in wallets and services, requiring timely updates for accuracy.  - Paxful should be removed, and Binance now shows evidence of supporting Taproot withdrawals.  - Regular updates and verification are crucial for maintaining reliable information about Taproot integration.

recent_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
recent_posts.summary: - The draft explains signer group design, focusing on key management and robust digital signature systems.  - It details operational rules, multi-round revocation, flexible closing, and splicing mechanisms.  - Open questions concern signature agreement thresholds, requiring further expert analysis on security guarantees.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal improves stale rate observability and network health diagnostics in Bitcoin.  - This optional P2P system enables nodes to share recent stale tip information using BIP 434 messages.  - Communication is limited to relevant tips, with strict data size restrictions and a 10-tip node cache.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary: - The draft proposes standardizing enforcement policies for co-signers to improve blockchain interoperability.  - It outlines unified policy formatting, verifications, and script-enforceable conditions for consistent application.  - Feedback is sought on technical aspects, including serialization methods, verification specifications, and draft placement.

active_posts.title: Three Bitcoin Core security advisories
active_posts.summary: - Three critical security vulnerabilities affecting Bitcoin Core have been identified and described in detail.  - These issues are resolved in Bitcoin Core version 29.2, subsequent 29.x, and version 30.0 onward.  - Users are strongly encouraged to upgrade to the latest supported releases for maximum security.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal identifies Bitcoin protocol vulnerabilities and suggests improvements for security and performance.  - Solutions include adjusting difficulty retargeting, limiting legacy transactions, and addressing Merkle root issues.  - Some proposed changes, like reducing block size, are debated due to concerns about scalability and functionality.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - Analysis of compact block reconstruction highlights the impact of transaction availability and node configuration changes.  - Network congestion, node-specific adjustments, and mempool policies significantly affect reconstruction efficiency and performance.  - Variations in reconstruction duration prompt further investigation into bandwidth, pool sizes, and node connection types.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - Integrating miniscript with taproot introduces challenges in creating unique, unspendable keys for wallet policies.  - Approaches include fixed unspendable xpubs, using random chaincodes, and recycling entropy from wallet descriptors.  - Each method has trade-offs in uniqueness, indistinguishability, and usability, requiring further refinement and discussion.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP - Block size doubles at each reward halving with max block size of 32M
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The draft proposes doubling the maximum block size at each block subsidy halving up to 32MB.  - Gradual increases plan to prevent overestimating future bandwidth and storage requirements.  - Non-upgraded clients will become incompatible, leading to network partitions after the first increase.

today_in_history_posts.title: Lightning, the death of BIP62, and Segregated Witness
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The author identified anchor malleability as a significant issue without BIP62 deployment.  - Different solutions were considered, but ultimately Segregated Witness was assumed to address malleability.  - Ignoring malleability simplifies lightning code, though future support may be challenging if required.

today_in_history_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The project revealed reduced convergence delays and identified inefficiencies in Lightning Network message propagation.  - Channel_update and node_announcement messages showed high repetition, suggesting implementation or filter issues.  - Future plans include expanding infrastructure, encouraging community involvement, and exploring public data release for analysis.
